draft.title: Concentration
card: Concentration is the amount of solute in a given amount of solution. Solute is the substance that dissolves. The volume used is that of the whole solution, not of the solvent alone.
Molar concentration is in mol/L: c = n ÷ V, with V in litres. Mass concentration is in g/L: mass of solute in grams ÷ volume of solution in litres.

Percentages: %(m/v) is grams of solute per 100 mL of solution. %(v/v) is millilitres of solute per 100 mL of solution. For very dilute solutions, ppm is used. 1 ppm is 1 mg of solute per litre of solution (mg/L) in water.
To convert between units, use the molar mass: g/L ÷ M = mol/L. For example, 58.5 g/L of NaCl is 1.00 mol/L, as M(NaCl) = 58.5 g/mol. Check that the volume is in the unit the formula needs.
draft.remember: Concentration is solute per volume of solution. Molar mass links g/L to mol/L.

a.q: A student dissolves 0.50 mol of sugar in water to make 250 mL of solution. What is the concentration in mol/L?
a.why: c = n ÷ V = 0.50 mol ÷ 0.250 L = 2.0 mol/L. Using 250 directly without converting to litres would give 125 mol/L, which is the mistake of leaving the volume in mL.
a.clue: Convert the volume to litres before dividing.

b.q: A saline solution contains 9.0 g/L of NaCl (M = 58.5 g/mol). Which is closest to its concentration in mol/L?
b.why: Divide the mass concentration by the molar mass: 9.0 ÷ 58.5 = 0.15 mol/L. Multiplying by the molar mass gives 527, and this reverses the conversion. 0.90 would come from treating 9.0 g/L as 0.90 g per 100 mL, which is not the conversion asked for.
b.clue: Moles are mass divided by molar mass.

problems.detail: The why says using 250 directly without converting to litres gives 125 mol/L. It does not: 0.50 ÷ 250 = 0.002 mol/L. 125 comes from multiplying 0.50 × 250. The why misdescribes the error behind that distractor and could confuse students checking their working.

check.summary: Both questions have the right answer (2.0 mol/L and 0.15 mol/L). The explanation for (a) wrongly says dividing by 250 mL gives 125 mol/L; that figure comes from multiplying, not dividing.
